_schema.purpose: Single canonical register of everything this project has measured, refuted, or left untried. Machine-readable source of truth; FINDINGS.md is GENERATED from it by findings.py and must never be hand-edited.

fields.kind: law | lever | dead_end | contradiction | untried | external
fields.claim: one sentence, falsifiable, stated as what is true
fields.magnitude: the number that matters, with units
fields.evidence: prereg number, file:line, or external source
fields.scope: the hardware and model class the claim was measured on - a claim outside its scope is a guess
fields.status: established | shipped | refuted | open | staked | untested
fields.wired_into: where it reaches shipped code, or null

untried_extra_fields.predicted_effect: staked magnitude - written BEFORE the test, so a miss is visible
untried_extra_fields.why_it_is_promising: which established finding implies this lever should work

laws.claim: THE DECODE WALL, measured basis: every active byte on a tier transits its bus once per token, so tok/s <= 1/sum(bytes_i/BW_i). On MEASURED bandwidth (26.1 GB/s pure-read stream, not the 48 spec) the flagship's raw-decode wall is 41.1 tok/s; we measure 22.25 (54%). The wall is EXCEEDABLE only by breaking the axiom: speculation verified 50.04 tok/s - 22% above it - in the copy regime.
laws.magnitude: Decomposition (prereg #27): stream measured 26.1 GB/s pure read / 30.4 copy, one thread already saturating; pure-CPU decode 14.06 tok/s = 17.1 GB/s effective = 66% of stream (kernel+MLP share); GPU<->CPU sync excess 7.4-11.1 ms/token = 17-25% of the token. The spec-sheet walls (69.5 / 52.9) were fiction: DDR4-3000 promises 48 GB/s this controller cannot deliver.
laws.evidence: prereg #27 (decomposition + measured stream), prereg #28 (the exceedance), prereg #25 (the 22.25)
laws.scope: reference box, flagship model. The axiom underneath is tier-agnostic: every active byte on a tier must transit that tier's bus once per token, so tok/s <= 1 / sum(bytes_i / BW_i). No runtime can beat that without reducing bytes or amortising them across tokens.
laws.wired_into: the research agenda: U-09 is the decomposition
laws.what_this_rules_in_and_out: RULED OUT: any raw-decode runtime gain past 1.85x on this box (41.1 ceiling), and in practice far less - the CPU path already runs at 66% of real stream, and sync is worth at most ~29%. D-05's no-fork verdict survives with that measured asterisk. RULED IN and MEASURED: exceeding the wall via speculation (50.04, prereg #28) and skipping prefill via prefix caching (29x TTFT, prereg #29). The remaining breakthroughs are not in moving bytes better - they are in not moving bytes at all.
laws.gap_attribution_final: The 22.25->41.1 gap is now FULLY attributed (prereg #31): ~40% is the MoE EXPERT-PATH CODE in ggml's CPU MUL_MAT_ID (prereg #32 REFUTED the prefetch story: shuffled 2MB slab reads lose nothing, and the MoE path saturates at 16 GB/s where dense reaches 28.4 identically threaded); 17-25% is GPU<->CPU sync (needs async transfer code, scheduling measured dead); 0% scheduling; 0% K-format choice (Q2_K and Q4_K_M tie at the wall on CPU). On stock llama.cpp this box's raw decode is FINISHED - every remaining percent costs upstream engineering bounded at 1.85x combined, while speculation already delivers 2.3-2.5x by not reading bytes at all.
laws.exceedance_record: The wall (41.1 tok/s raw decode on measured bandwidth) is now exceeded by 2.2x: 90.33 tok/s with ngram speculation at size-m 384 (prereg #36), byte-identical output. The remaining ceiling is the batched verify forward, measured at ~405-445 tok/s (#26) - so speculation itself still runs at ~1/4.5 of ITS ceiling, and the binding constraint there is draft availability from the n-gram store, not hardware.
laws.cpu_tier_closed_by_direct_measurement: prereg #49: the CPU expert path moves 0.516 GB in 18.45 ms = 28.0 GB/s, above the 26.1 GB/s numpy pure-read stream and matching the 30.4 GB/s copy figure. Previously inferred (#27/#33); now measured per-op on a CUDA build. The CPU tier has nothing left.

laws.claim: THE PREFILL WALL. Batched prefill converges to ~405-445 t/s on this GPU regardless of placement - 65-67% of the card's theoretical FLOP ceiling, which is as close as real kernels get on Pascal. Prefill on this box is CLOSED except for levers that cut FLOPs themselves.
laws.magnitude: GTX 1060 6GB ~4.4 TFLOPS FP32; MoE k=8 active 3.3B -> ~6.6 GFLOP/token -> 667 t/s at 100%. Measured convergence: 443.82 (split), 425.31 (all-CPU), 405.22 (dense control) at npl=8 - three different placements, one ceiling. The only measured lever that moves it is top-k reduction, which cuts the FLOPs: +21% to +63% at k=4 (prereg #22).
laws.evidence: prereg #26 (the convergence), prereg #22 (the FLOP lever)
laws.scope: GTX 1060. A modern GPU has 10-100x the FLOPs; this wall is a property of the card, not of llama.cpp.
laws.wired_into: the research agenda: asymmetric top-k Stage 2 (U-07) is the one open prefill lever

laws.claim: ACCEPTANCE DECAY SEPARATES DRAFTERS. A copy drafter's acceptance is ~flat in draft length; a model drafter's collapses geometrically - so the same 'raise the budget' fix that multiplies one destroys the other.
laws.magnitude: n-gram (copy): 66-68% acceptance at 384-token drafts, and raising the budget 48->384 gave +81% throughput (#36). Draft model (0.6B guessing): 75.2% -> 56.8% -> 34.9% on code and 35.9% -> 17.6% -> 8.7% on prose as the budget goes 3 -> 8 -> 16, and throughput falls monotonically (#42). An n-gram draft is verified-correct BY CONSTRUCTION - it reproduces text that occurred - so extending it is nearly free; a model draft compounds its own divergence AND pays a full draft forward per token.
laws.evidence: prereg #36 (n-gram budget), prereg #42 (draft-model budget), prereg #28 (the original net-negative)
laws.scope: Qwen3-30B-A3B target with a Qwen3-0.6B draft, reference box. The mechanism is general; the crossover point is not measured elsewhere.
laws.wired_into: quantprobe/plan.py:speculation_advice (why the two speculation flags behave oppositely)

laws.claim: The VRAM tier's bandwidth ceiling is eta 0.84 measured independently; llama.cpp's quantized decode reaches 0.513 at Q4_K_M. The 1.64x gap is NOT hardware and NOT arithmetic - sm_61 uses native __dp4a INT8 at ~4x the fp32 rate, and the fp32 GEMV was already bandwidth-bound.
laws.magnitude: CuPy on GTX 1060 6GB: pure read 165.6 GB/s (eta 0.86), copy 150.1 (0.78), decode-shaped fp32 GEMV (1x4096)@(4096x14336) 161.3 GB/s (eta 0.84), GEMV within 2.6% of pure read so it is bandwidth-bound and the comparison is valid. llama.cpp all-in-VRAM implies eta 0.32-0.56 (C-02). FORMAT LADDER (same session): llama.cpp all-in-VRAM eta climbs monotonically with bits - Q2_K 0.311, IQ3_XS 0.332, IQ3_M 0.343, Q4_K_M 0.513 - consistent with dequantisation cost, and Q4_K_M's 98.6 GB/s is 91% of the independent fp16 ceiling (108.9) but only 61% of the fp32 one (161.3).
laws.evidence: prereg #44
laws.scope: GTX 1060 6GB (Pascal sm_61), fp32. NOT established for quantized kernels - see the caveat below.
laws.wired_into: findings/REGISTER.json:C-02 (reclassified) - deliberately NOT wired into plan.py: the tool's eta constants describe what llama.cpp achieves, which is what users get, and must not be raised to a ceiling no shipped runtime reaches.
laws.the_caveat_that_bounds_it: cuBLAS fp32 GEMV and llama.cpp's quantized decode are NOT the same operation - llama.cpp streams Q2_K/Q4_K blocks and dequantises in-kernel, work cuBLAS never does. The fp16 row is the warning: 108.9 GB/s vs fp32's 161.3, because Pascal's fp16 ALU runs at 1/64 rate. On this architecture the arithmetic format can bind before bandwidth does. So 0.84 is the CEILING; how much a quantized kernel can reach is unmeasured.
laws.the_open_question: Which ceiling applies depends on the arithmetic ggml's quantized CUDA kernels use on sm_61 (dequantize_mul_mat_vec vs MMQ paths). That is a SOURCE question, answerable with no hardware, and it decides whether the GPU-side prize is 1.1x (not worth pursuing) or 1.64x (worth an upstream PR).
laws.arithmetic_question_closed: Answered from source: common.cuh:51 defines GGML_CUDA_CC_DP4A=610 and :722 selects __dp4a when __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 610. The GTX 1060 is sm_61 = 610 exactly, so the quantized path uses native INT8 DP4A. The fp16 comparand (108.9 GB/s) does NOT apply and the 1.1x floor it implied is withdrawn. The remaining explanation is the kernel's unpacking/scale work - real work cuBLAS never does - and whether it is reducible is unmeasured.
laws.revision_history: This figure moved three times in one session: 1.5-2.6x (fp32 comparand, unexamined) -> 1.1-1.64x (fp16 comparand raised) -> 1.64x (arithmetic determined from source). Each move came from checking a comparand rather than defending the previous number.

laws.claim: Law 4 AMENDED: eta is a function of the FORMAT's unpack instruction cost, not the tier alone. A matvec with no unpacking runs at 95% of the streaming ceiling; the same bytes with a naive unpack run at 42%; dp4a recovers 80%. On an ALU-weak GPU the format sets decode speed as much as the byte count. [AMENDED by prereg #70: the IQ ladder is measured - IQ2_XS 51.1 / IQ3_S 61.1 / IQ3_XXS 68.3 / IQ4_NL 117.0 ebw on the same card, same session. The divide is CODEBOOK vs not, not IQ vs K: codebook formats pay their grid lookup in decode (36-52% below Q4_K per byte) while IQ4_NL's kernel is Q4_0-class and lands beside Q4_0 (117 vs 119.1). 'IQ is slow' is scoped to codebook formats.]
laws.magnitude: Same tier, same card, same model, same session: Q4_0 eta 0.619 vs Q4_K_M 0.553 vs Q2_K 0.340. Bare-metal ladder (own CUDA, zero llama.cpp): no-unpack 152.5 GB/s (0.79 spec), naive 4.5-bit 67.8 (0.35), dp4a 4.5-bit 128.7-132.1 (0.67-0.69), stream 161.0 (0.84).
laws.evidence: prereg #52, prereg #53, tools/kernelprobe/bench.cu (every kernel correctness-checked vs double host reference); prereg #56 NARROWS the mechanism: at real 1-row geometry with dp4a, marginal instruction differences (min term, packed scales) cost <=5% - the naive-float->dp4a 1.9x remains the proven instruction effect, and the residual K-quant e2e deficit is attributed to layout/occupancy, OPEN; prereg #70 IQ ladder
laws.scope: measured on ONE Pascal card (cc 6.1); on Ampere+ the ALU/BW ratio flips and the ranking may invert - unverified, replication asked
laws.wired_into: quantprobe/plan.py format_advice; GROK_KERNEL_BRIEF.md; explains C-05 (6 prior sightings, mechanism now named)

laws.claim: THE K-QUANT DEFICIT MECHANISM: metadata application DENSITY. A format that defines scale+min per 16 weights forces a metadata FMA chain every 4 bytes at 2 bits - 4x the application density of Q4_K per byte. Confirmation arm with identical loads and identical dp4a count, scale applied per-u32 instead of per-quad: 83.8 -> 103.2 GB/s (+23%). Full decomposition of real Q2_K: 131 (Q4_K-class ceiling) x0.64 (density) x0.885 (e2e dilution) = 74 vs 65.4 measured - 88% accounted; Q4_K 91% accounted. The deficit is intrinsic to the format DEFINITION because quality at 2 bits requires exactly the fine asymmetric metadata that costs the density (quality.py: every coarser/symmetric variant loses).
laws.magnitude: +23% density arm; residuals 9-12% unattributed (occupancy / q8_1-struct walk)
laws.evidence: prereg #57 (incl. exploratory density arm, labeled post-hoc), prereg #56, quality.py ladder
laws.scope: one Pascal card; the density cost shrinks wherever ALU/BW ratio is higher
laws.wired_into: quantprobe/plan.py format_advice; GROK_KERNEL_BRIEF.md; C-02 closure

laws.claim: THE SPLIT PLACEMENT LAW: GPU device time = format tax (L-16) + a per-call floor (~16 us/call on this WDDM Pascal box, in-kernel not submission - CUDA graphs +3.2% independently confirm). One model reconciles both measured arms: all-in-VRAM 7B predicted 48.3 vs 45.8 measured (+5%); flagship split predicted 23.7 vs 23.9 (-1%). The split eta 0.15 vs 0.34 is CALL GRANULARITY - 2.5x the calls on 4.2x fewer GPU bytes explodes the floor share from ~12% to ~58%. Fix direction is fewer/bigger calls (speculation verify batches, more resident expert layers, shared activation quantization), not kernel code. [DOWNGRADED 2026-07-28 by prereg #59, own kill rule: out-of-sample test on two unseen models FAILED. 0.5B measured 153.96 vs predicted ~100 (floor is size-dependent, ~4us on tiny kernels vs the fitted 16); DeepSeek-Lite MLA split measured 16.26 vs predicted ~21.1 (a missing term). The DIRECTION survives - byte-only over-predicts both, by +23% and +73% - but the single-constant form is a two-point fit, not a law. NOT wired into plan.py.]
laws.magnitude: 853 vs 341 GPU nodes/token; matmuls 80% of split device time running 5-15x their byte cost per call; known floor contributor: q8_1 activation re-quantization inside every quantized matmul (~1.5-3 ms/token)
laws.evidence: prereg #58 (E9 per-op attribution, reconciled 96.9%/99.1% against E6), prereg #48 (graphs null), prereg #50 (E6 baseline); prereg #59 (out-of-sample test: FAILED, kill rule honoured); prereg #64 REVISES the #59 DS-Lite attribution: at healthy clocks DS measures 23.08, inside its staked band - that miss was substantially the stuck-boost state. The L-17 kill stands on the 0.5B arm alone.
laws.scope: one Pascal/WDDM box, batch 1; the floor constant is machine-specific, the LAW (floor x calls + format tax) should transfer
laws.wired_into: quantprobe plan.py eta constants gain mechanistic justification; preregistrations/2026-07-28-split-eta-attribution.md

laws.claim: The all-in-VRAM efficiency spread is a PROPERTY OF THE POPULATION, not a Pascal artefact and not an architecture constant. On one basis (eta against file bytes / spec bandwidth), 61 public benchmarks across 8 GPU architectures span 0.512 (hopper) to 0.812 (rdna4), median 0.62 - a 1.6x spread - and our own Pascal box (0.509-0.577 measured) sits INSIDE that range, not below it. Consequence: no per-architecture constant can replace the one-sided floor; the variance is irreducible from public data and only a per-machine measurement (calibrate's anchors) collapses it. The 'typically 1.1-1.8x above the floor' disclosure is therefore externally validated, not a hedge.
laws.magnitude: 1.6x population spread; Pascal inside it; floor + calibrate both justified by external data
laws.evidence: prereg #72 (killed as specified, scored before implementation); weights/data/public_bench_corpus.json (61 entries, weights/public_bench_audit.py); E-08 (RTX 5070 at eta_file 0.810, the population maximum)
laws.scope: dense Q4-class all-in-VRAM decode, spec-bandwidth basis; MoE-resident rows have a thinner corpus (0.31-0.50) and are NOT covered by this claim
laws.wired_into: plan.py fits_in_vram_advice floor language (evidence line); README/LAWS floor section

laws.claim: Law 4 v2's context term is a BANDWIDTH model, and that is only true where attention runs on the GPU. Measured at 4k/16k/32k (prereg #73): all-in-VRAM is exact (-0.9% at d4096) and MoE expert-splits stay in band at every depth to 32k (-10% to -23%) because a MoE split keeps attention and KV in VRAM and offloads only expert FFNs. DENSE splits, which put whole layers including attention on the CPU, break: +182% over at d16384 and +381% at d32768. The missing cost is CPU-side attention over the whole KV cache each token - compute on N threads, not a byte read - and it is measured at 1.43 us/position/layer at d16k and 1.42 at d32k (two depths, 1% apart) on this box's 4 threads. [TERM VALIDATED OUT-OF-SAMPLE, prereg #74: k = 1.43 (7B/8L/d16k) / 1.42 (7B/11L/d32k) / 1.76 (14B/30L/d8k) us per position per CPU layer - one constant across two models, 8-30 CPU layers, 8k-32k depth. Shipped as the mean 1.55e-6; the dense-split-at-depth regime now carries a priced prediction instead of a refusal.] [EXTENDED to pure CPU, prereg #75: staked 1.1 and measured 1.38 (band edge, under-promise), and the ranking inversion is fixed (pure CPU 1.38 < dense split 3.44 at the same depth). Implied k there is 1.10 us - LOWER than the split arms (no GPU hand-off, threads keep their cache), so the shipped 1.55 mean runs ~40% pessimistic on pure CPU. Four arms now span k = 1.10-1.76 us: a first-order correction, not a precision instrument.]
laws.magnitude: context term validated to 32k for GPU-attention placements; refuted for dense CPU splits (1.4 us/pos/layer)
laws.evidence: prereg #73 (weights/data/prereg73_kv_depth.log); re-explains prereg #66's -58% dense-split-at-16k arm as this class; prereg #74 (out-of-sample holdout, weights/data/prereg74_cpu_attention.log); prereg #75 (pure-CPU limiting case, first ever measured in this project)
laws.scope: this box (4 threads, PCIe3, Pascal); the constant is thread-count and CPU dependent, the SHAPE (linear in depth x CPU layers) is the claim
laws.wired_into: quantprobe/plan.py depth_scope_warning; LAWS.md Law 4 v2 scope

laws.claim: Effective decode bandwidth is f(FORMAT, ROWS-PER-TENSOR, BYTES-PER-ROW) - geometry has TWO independent axes, and format is only the third. Measured on one card with everything else constant (preregs #80/#81): (1) ROWS/TENSOR sets the approach to the ceiling - 4.5-bit weights run 31.0 GB/s at 128 rows and 100.5 at 16384, monotone, 3.2x, with the knee at ~4096 rows; (2) that knee is INVARIANT to row width (same 4096 rows at 1152 and at 2304 bytes/row), so it is a grid-size / occupancy floor, not launch-overhead amortisation - any shape term must be keyed on ROWS; (3) BYTES-PER-ROW sets where the ceiling IS - doubling row width raised the saturated bandwidth from 98.7 to 138.5 GB/s (+40%). CONSEQUENCE: every FORMAT_EBW entry carries TWO hidden variables from the model it was measured on - the FFN shape and that model's row width - and is an upper bound on both counts. Same physics as L-19 (CPU attention at depth) and #59 (small-model size floor), at tensor granularity.
laws.magnitude: 3.2x by rows/tensor; +40% ceiling by bytes/row; attention-shaped work -23% vs FFN-shaped at fixed width, which explains prereg #79's failure (r=0.87)
laws.evidence: prereg #80 (shape sweep) + prereg #81 (K-invariance: the knee is a row count, the ceiling is not); tools/kernelprobe/shape.cu; weights/data/prereg80_shape.log, prereg81_knee.log
laws.scope: Pascal, batch-1 decode geometry (one output row per block, #55). The two-axis SHAPE is the claim; knee position and ceiling gain are per-card and unmeasured elsewhere.
laws.wired_into: findings only - deliberately NOT in the tool: a table keyed on rows alone would bake our 7B's row width into every prediction as an invisible constant, the exact error class this day has been about. Needs U-29's per-architecture read sets to supply both keys.

laws.claim: THE SMALL-MODEL SIZE FLOOR IS NON-MATMUL OVERHEAD SHARE, measured for the first time from inside a real decode (instrumented build, GGML_GPU_PROFILE_OPS, prereg #83). A token is not only weight reads: RMS_NORM, ROPE, FLASH_ATTN_EXT, SET_ROWS and GET_ROWS cost real GPU time, and the normalisation ops cost the SAME absolute time regardless of model size - RMS_NORM measured 15.28 us/call on a 0.5B and 15.52 us/call on a 7B, a 1.6% difference across a 15x model-size range. Against 10x fewer weight bytes that fixed cost becomes a large share of the token: MUL_MAT is 91.6% of GPU device time on the 7B but only 73.0% on the 0.5B, i.e. non-matmul overhead is 8.4% vs 27.0%. Law 4 models weight bytes only, so it necessarily mis-prices whichever end of that range it was not calibrated on - which is exactly #59's size floor and exactly why one anchor cannot price a 100x size range. [CORRECTED SAME DAY by four more profiles - my 'size-invariant' claim was an artifact of measuring TWO MODELS OF ONE FAMILY. Across six models RMS_NORM costs 15.27 and 15.51 us/call on the two Qwen2.5 models (invariant WITHIN the family, as claimed) but 9.30 / 8.26 / 7.72 us/call on Qwen3-0.6B / Qwen3.5-4B / gemma4-12B - a 2x spread ACROSS families. The per-op cost is architecture-specific, not universal. What survives: the OVERHEAD SHARE is large and falls with model size - 27.0% (0.5B) / 22.3% (0.6B) / 19.6% (4B) / 14.2% (gemma-12B) / 8.4% (7B) - so Law 4's bytes-only model still mis-prices whichever end it was not calibrated on. But the share is not a clean function of size either (the 4.7GB 7B sits at 8.4% while the 5.2GB gemma sits at 14.2%, and gemma's FLASH_ATTN costs 134.7 us/call against the 7B's 78.7), so any overhead term must be per-architecture, measured, not a single constant.] [SECOND CORRECTION, same data, U-33: the overhead SHARES above are UPPER BOUNDS inflated by the profiler itself. The instrumented build records a CUDA event pair per op; comparing its tg32 against the clean ladder tg32 for the same four files gives 3.80-8.32 us of instrumentation per op call - the SAME ORDER as the 5-16 us op times it reports. With 124-373 launch-bound calls per token that is 0.5-3.1 ms, i.e. 30-100% of the non-matmul bucket it claims to measure. The 8.4%-27.0% range is therefore not a clean measurement of overhead, and the direction of the bias is worst exactly where call counts are highest - the small models the law is about.] [THIRD CORRECTION, prereg #85, and this one has a number: the launch cost was measured WITHOUT per-op instrumentation - one CUDA event pair around N launches instead of N event pairs. laws.claim: THE TIER MODEL INVERTS FOR KV: WEIGHTS CAN BE TIERED BECAUSE THEY ARE RE-USED ACROSS TOKENS; KV CANNOT, BECAUSE AT DECODE IT IS RE-READ IN FULL EVERY TOKEN. The tiered waterfall prices WEIGHTS by reuse - a MoE token reads only the active fraction (qwen3-30b: ~3.3B active of 30.5B total), the same experts recur across tokens, so an LRU cache gives the stream a MISS RATE a faster tier can absorb (plan.py's own miss arithmetic puts the RAM-served share of a stream row's active bytes at ~30-93% across the preset grid, rising with the RAM:model ratio - 31-63% on the 16GB reference box, model-dependent; BigMoeOnEdge measures 76-84% dynamic hot-expert hit rates on device, U-34, and streams a ~60GB model off a 12GB phone's flash at 2.2 tok/s best-of) and slow storage serves only the misses. The KV cache has NO such asymmetry: attention reads EVERY past position EVERY generated token, so there is no hot subset, no miss rate, and nothing for a cache to skip - the cache IS the working set and it is fully re-read each step. Four consequences. (a) Moving KV one tier down costs ~LINEARLY in the bandwidth ratio with zero cache relief: our own -nkvo A/B measures 3.04x worse than q8_0 KV in VRAM at d16384 (3.48 vs 10.59 tok/s tg32, V-08, advice line shipped per prereg #25's pre-commitment). (b) STREAMING KV from SSD at decode is strictly worse than RAM and degrades further with context, because the full re-read multiplies every added position by the slowest bus with no miss-rate term to dampen it - this clause is priced out by arithmetic on measured bus ratios, not by a direct measurement. (c) The levers that DO work on KV are SHRINK - q8_0 KV, +37% at d16384 (prereg #25), at no measurable quality cost up to the deepest depth f16 can even run (prereg #91, L-24) - and READ-LESS - eviction/sparse attention (StreamingLLM, H2O, SnapKV), UNMEASURED by this project. (d) SSD is legitimate for KV exactly once: PREFIX PERSISTENCE, where a saved prompt cache is read ONCE at load - a TTFT lever in the same family as the measured 29x cache_prompt reuse (prereg #29) - never a decode lever. Boundary evidence that SHRINK is sometimes not even optional: f16 KV at -c 8192 on Qwen3-30B-A3B Q2_K with split placement CUDA-OOMs on this 6GB card while the q8_0 arm completes (session run of 2026-07-30 reported PPL 7.7926 for the q8 arm at 8192; that log was overwritten by the round-2 -c 7168 re-run, so the retained artifacts are exp56's 7168 logs plus the shipped script's own probe comment encoding that 8192 OOMs for f16) - at that model/card/depth, q8_0 KV is not an optimization, it is ENABLING.

laws.claim: PERPLEXITY IS BLUNT WHERE KL DIVERGENCE IS SHARP, AND WE HAVE BEEN THROWING THE SHARP ONE AWAY. llama.cpp's --kl-divergence already reports the full KLD distribution (Maximum, 99.9, 99, 95, 90, Median and the low tail) plus 'Same top p' - the share of positions where the quantized model still picks the same argmax - on the SAME forward passes we already run for perplexity. quantprobe reported only perplexity. Measured on one graded pair (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, Q8_0 reference logits, arms requantized to Q4_K_M and Q2_K, wikitext2, 6 chunks): perplexity 14.49 -> 17.77, a ratio of 1.23x that reads as '23% worse'. Over the same pair KLD median moved 7.77x, KLD p99 6.70x, and SAME-TOP-P fell from 90.0% to 72.6% - the Q2_K model picks a DIFFERENT TOKEN on 27.4% of positions. A 23% perplexity regression and a 27% change in what the model actually says are not the same sentence. CORRECTION TO THE HYPOTHESIS THAT MOTIVATED THE EXPERIMENT, published because the framing is what generalises: this was staked as 'damage hides in the TAIL, so measure p99'. THE TAIL IS NOT SPECIAL. KLD median moved 7.77x against p99's 6.70x - the whole distribution shifts together and the percentile choice barely matters for comparing quants. The staked P1 passed (tail/mean 5.46x against a 1.5x threshold) but it passed for the wrong reason: the win is KL-versus-PERPLEXITY, not tail-versus-mean. The distribution IS heavy-tailed within an arm (p99/median 8-9x, P3 as staked) but no shipped claim rests on the tail being privileged.

NOT established: that these ratios hold at other sizes or architectures, or for MoE (routing damage may behave unlike dense weight damage); and NOT established that KLD predicts task-level performance - it measures divergence from the reference, the right question for a QUANTIZATION tool and the wrong one for ranking models. laws.claim: MMAP COSTS 1.39x AGAINST read() FOR STREAMING, AND ACCESS GRANULARITY COSTS FAR MORE THAN ACCESS PATTERN EVER DID. Prereg #99, a 2x2 of {read(), mmap+page-touch} x {sequential, scattered} on one 37 GB GGUF, disjoint fixed cold regions, every arm moving exactly 2 GB: read sequential 0.5501 GB/s, mmap sequential 0.3962 (1.388x slower), read scattered at 4 KB 0.0300 (18.3x slower than sequential read), mmap scattered at 4 KB 0.0107 (51.4x). P1 SUPPORTED as staked: page-fault overhead is real and sequential mmap is materially slower than sequential read on the same file and drive. BUT THE STAKED HYPOTHESIS IS THE SMALLER HALF OF WHAT THIS FOUND. D-28 concluded 'this drive does not care about access pattern' from 512 MB units; at 4 KB units the pattern is catastrophic - 18x for read() and 51x for mmap. D-28 is not wrong, it is SCOPED to its granularity, and that scope was not stated at the time. Granularity, not pattern, is the variable that matters. HOW MUCH OF C-23 THIS EXPLAINS: llama.cpp streams at 0.2505 GB/s effective (exp96b); against THIS run's sequential read baseline that is a 2.20x total gap, of which mmap accounts for 1.388x, leaving 1.58x UNEXPLAINED. So mmap is a real but PARTIAL answer and C-23 does not close here.
laws.magnitude: mmap/read 1.388x sequential; 4 KB granularity 18.3x (read) and 51.4x (mmap) vs sequential read
laws.evidence: weights/exp99_mmap_vs_read.py (stake in the module docstring), weights/data/exp99_mmap_vs_read.json
laws.scope: One drive (SATA SSD), one file, 2 GB per arm, Python page-touch as the mmap consumer. CAVEAT NOT TO BE BURIED: this run's sequential-read arm measured 0.5501 GB/s while D-28 measured 0.452-0.459 on the same drive - 1.21x apart, from a different region and span and possibly partial caching. Ratios WITHIN this run are sound; absolute numbers must NOT be compared across the two experiments, and the 2.20x total gap above inherits that uncertainty. The 4 KB arms are a granularity FLOOR, not a model of llama.cpp: llama.cpp reads tensors, which are large contiguous blocks, so it almost certainly does not pay the 18x/51x penalties - they bound what a naive page-granular reader would suffer. KR-A passed decisively (warm mmap re-touch 25.75 GB/s), which also bounds Python interpreter overhead at 1.5% of the cold mmap arm - the one way this design could have manufactured a fake mmap penalty. Contention biases every ratio toward 1.0, i.e. AGAINST the result obtained, so 1.388x is a lower bound.
laws.wired_into: nothing yet, and the next step is a PREDICTION rather than a coefficient. llama.cpp exposes --no-mmap; if page-fault overhead is what this measures, --no-mmap should buy a measurable fraction of 1.388x on a model that FITS RAM. That is directly testable and it is the next experiment. Note the limitation honestly: --no-mmap needs the model to fit in RAM, so it cannot help the disk tier - exactly the tier where C-23's gap hurts most. U-23 already gates --no-mmap advice on RAM headroom; this would quantify the benefit behind that gate. Law 4 keeps pricing DEVICE bandwidth and the disk tier keeps its disclosed 30% pessimism until the unexplained 1.58x is accounted for.

levers.claim: N-gram speculation is worth ~4.7x on copy-regime output AT ~3-BIT QUANTIZATION - and the multiplier SHRINKS with bits (3.39x at Q3_K_M), because speculation converts a bandwidth-bound problem into a compute-bound one.
levers.magnitude: Flagship, split placement, chat template, coherent output (prereg #28): edit task 2.41x (20.73 -> 50.04 tok/s, 89% acceptance) - ABOVE the 41.1 raw-decode wall; novel code 0.98x at 0% acceptance; novel prose 1.00x. Dense 7B (original): 2.10x on code. The original 'code vs prose' framing was a proxy: code tasks are usually copy-heavy and prose tasks usually novel, but the edit IS the variable. Also measured: the staked temp-0 raw-continuation harness produced a repetition loop whose 100% acceptance inflated ngram to 1.82-1.96x on garbage output - caught by reading the completion, re-measured under the chat template. COMPOSITION (prereg #35): speculation and q8_0 KV are independent multipliers - stack measured 49.42 vs 47.61 predicted from the product (ratio 1.038, no destructive interference), and output is byte-identical at both KV precisions. DRAFT-LENGTH SWEEP (prereg #36, position-controlled): --spec-ngram-simple-size-m 24/48/96/192/384/768 -> 46.10 / 49.80 / 65.00 / 78.01 / 90.33 / 89.82 tok/s, ALL byte-identical output. Best is m=384 at 90.33 = +81% over the default and 2.2x this box's raw-decode wall. Mechanism: m is a per-round draft BUDGET, so raising it delivers the SAME accepted tokens in FEWER verify rounds (drafted/accepted freeze at 1100/735 from m=192 on while throughput still climbs) - each round costs a full weight read. m=768 returns byte-identical counts to m=384 because the n-gram store has no longer matching spans: the plateau is the DRAFTER's ceiling, not the hardware's. LOOKUP-LENGTH SWEEP (prereg #37, position-controlled, all at size-m 384): size-n 20/12/6/4/2 -> 77.61 / 90.67 / 105.52 / 108.41 / 81.98 tok/s, all byte-identical. Best is n=4 at 108.41 = 5.0x the 21.6 no-speculation baseline and 2.6x the 41.1 raw-decode wall. Stacking ngram-cache is a 10% REGRESSION (97.16).
levers.evidence: prereg #10 (Law 6 arm S-e, dense), prereg #28 (flagship, re-scoped); prereg #36 (draft-length sweep); prereg #37 (lookup length + stacking); prereg #40 (quality scoping, with same-model confound control)
levers.scope: llama-server only - llama-cli silently ignores --spec-type (measured as a 1.00x that was the flag not existing) QUANTIZATION SCOPE (prereg #40): the multiplier is NOT invariant in bits. Same model (Qwen3-Coder-30B): Q2_K_L 4.63x, Q3_K_M 3.39x = 0.73 of it. Two different models at ~10.5 GB both give 4.6-4.8x, so bits is the variable, not the model.
levers.counterintuitive_note: Acceptance rate is the WRONG optimisation target. It FALLS from 100% (m=24) to 66.8% (m=384) while throughput rises from 46 to 90 tok/s. Rejected drafts are nearly free; skipped weight reads are not. Anyone tuning speculation by maximising acceptance will tune it backwards.
levers.the_hidden_variable: Across n=20->4 drafted tokens move only +5% (1068->1121) while throughput moves +40%. Tokens drafted is not the variable; VERIFY ROUNDS are - the same drafted tokens delivered in fewer, longer runs, each round costing one full weight read. Confirmed independently in #36 (throughput rose while drafted/accepted froze). Neither draft_n nor acceptance measures it. n=2 is the proof: it drafts the MOST (1486) and accepts the most (775) and is 25% SLOWER than n=4, because a 2-token lookup matches noise and produces many short quickly-rejected runs.
levers.identity_scope_note: Temp-0 identity claims in this project compare MATCHED REQUEST INDEX. Measured in prereg #38: request 1 and request 2 of the same server produce different output (sha 65985276565a vs 28a5c1e1c014) with AND without speculation - that is prompt-cache reuse (cache_prompt defaults true; reused KV is not bit-identical to freshly computed KV), not a speculation effect. Across arms at the same request index, every speculation configuration is byte-identical. Earlier harnesses reported only the last request's sha, so they were comparing req2 to req2 - valid, but blind to this.
levers.context_floor_trap: ngram-simple cannot draft until cur_len > size_m + size_n + 1 (ngram-map.cpp:65). Our shipped m=384/n=4 therefore has a 389-TOKEN CONTEXT FLOOR: on short prompts it does nothing at all, strictly worse than llama.cpp's default (61-token floor). Found in prereg #41 only because a short-prompt novel test forced it; every copy-regime measurement used a ~950-token prompt and cleared the bar invisibly.
levers.identity_claim_corrected: CORRECTION (prereg #41): 'byte-identical by construction' is FALSE and this project asserted it repeatedly. Speculation is output-preserving in EXACT arithmetic; in floating point a verify pass evaluates several positions in one batched forward, and batched reductions are not bit-identical to single-token decode, so at temp 0 an argmax can flip. Measured: the default drafter on a novel-code task drafted 38 tokens, accepted ZERO, and still produced different output - reproducibly (sha 1c2a7a785d on both runs). Every copy-regime comparison we ran WAS byte-identical, which is real evidence but not a guarantee.

dead_ends.claim: THE ACCESS-PATTERN EXPLANATION FOR THE DISK-TIER MISS IS DEAD, AND KILLING IT CONFIRMED THE DISK CALIBRATION IS CORRECT. C-21 measured the disk tier 30% faster than predicted and named two candidate causes it could not separate: H1 the probe's random-offset draw under-reports what sequential streaming achieves, or H2 the page-cache miss fraction is lower than modelled. Prereg #94 staked the discriminator BEFORE running, with the inconclusive band declared in advance (>=1.30x supports H1, <=1.10x refutes it, between is claimed by neither) so the answer could not be chosen for convenience. RESULT: scattered reads (8 x 512 MB at random offsets) 0.452 GB/s; one contiguous 4 GB read 0.459 GB/s; ratio 1.015x. H1 REFUTED - this drive does not care about access pattern at this size. THE MORE VALUABLE HALF IS THE POSITIVE ONE: both arms land within 4% of the 0.47 GB/s that `quantprobe calibrate` measures, so the C-17-corrected disk figure is now INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED by a probe with a working falsifier - the cannot-vary guard read 2.802 GB/s on a warm re-read, well clear of its 2.0 threshold, proving the harness distinguishes RAM from disk rather than emitting a constant. The v1.24.0 changelog said 'proving the old number wrong is not the same as proving the new one right'; the new one is now right. BY ELIMINATION C-21's 30% MISS BELONGS TO THE MISS FRACTION: the law assumes 0.637 of each token's bytes are re-read from disk, and the measurement implies ~0.429. That is what expert-usage skew predicts - if MoE routing concentrates on a hot subset, those experts stay page-cached permanently and never pay disk.

Same model all-in-VRAM, eta rises with bits (0.311 Q2_K -> 0.513 Q4_K_M) because fewer bits means more unpacking per delivered byte - so Q4_K_M carries 55% MORE bytes than Q2_K and is still faster (22.60 vs 21.26 tok/s).

contradictions.claim: quantprobe SUMS multi-device bandwidth, which models tensor-parallel (--split-mode row). llama.cpp's DEFAULT is --split-mode LAYER, which is SERIAL - so for any multi-GPU user on defaults the tool over-predicts decode by roughly the device count.
contradictions.magnitude: agg_bw() returns sum(v)*eff for a device list (quantprobe/plan.py). Under a layer split each GPU holds a disjoint subset of layers and they run SEQUENTIALLY within a token, so t = sum(bytes_i/BW_i): two IDENTICAL cards give the same decode speed as one card that could hold everything - capacity, not bandwidth. The tool would predict ~2x. For HETEROGENEOUS cards it is worse than wrong in magnitude, it is wrong in DIRECTION: adding a slow card to a fast one makes a fitting model SLOWER (3090 alone 1.30 ms/token vs 3090+1060 at 20/80 = 2.31 ms), while the tool predicts a gain.

contradictions.claim: CALIBRATION HAS NO COMPLETENESS CONTRACT, AND PARTIAL CALIBRATION IS WORSE THAN NONE FOR THE COMPONENTS YOU SKIPPED. Found via five full ladder runs on 2026-07-31 while chasing an unrelated (real, reboot-recoverable) machine slowdown; the GPU-only control row measured 153.39/153.74/153.00/152.95/152.08 across all five states, so the card is the fixed point. THREE SHIPPED DEFECTS. (1) Nothing ever re-measures: calibration is written to ~/.quantprobe/calibration.json and read back forever, only an explicit 'quantprobe calibrate' re-measures, so a user who calibrates once during a degraded window carries it silently (measured cost: median 8.8% -> 9.9%, every error flipping sign). (2) A MISSING file degrades SILENTLY to presets rather than re-measuring - 'machine state: uncalibrated (ram None GB/s)' in a line nobody must read - producing a 27.2% median on a healthy machine, while the calibrated case gets a prominent [calibrated] tag and the uncalibrated case gets none. (3) THE NON-OBVIOUS ONE: calibrating RAM alone made the RAM-bound rows the most accurate ever recorded here (Qwen3-30B-A3B -10.2% -> +1.6%, Coder-30B -10.0% -> +0.9%) while wrecking every GPU-bound row (0.5B -18.6% -> -28.1%, gemma4-12B 0.0% -> +12.8%, Qwen3.6-APEX-MTP +8.5% -> +42.0%), net median 12.5% - WORSE than the 8.8% baseline it replaced. Calibration is a VECTOR whose presets are mutually consistent, each compensating for the others' biases; measuring one component and leaving the rest on presets breaks that consistency and the damage lands on exactly the components you did NOT measure. Restoring the full vector (ram 24.14, disk 2.99, decode anchor) gave a 7.9% median, beating the 8.8% baseline. SEPARATE FOURTH DEFECT: the disk-only probe read 0.46 GB/s where the full calibration measured 2.99 GB/s on the same drive in the same session (+550%) - every disk-tier prediction under cal 75eb1d48, which shipped 0.45, rested on it; cause undiagnosed, cold-cache/first-touch suspected.

Two staked calls scored at equal prominence: 'an idle machine will restore the MoE rows' REFUTED (30B measured 17.51 idle-gated, and the Qwen3.6 rows got SLOWER at idle than under load); 'a reboot will restore them' CONFIRMED (21.10 immediately post-reboot, 21.56 on the final full calibration, against a 21.71 baseline).
contradictions.wired_into: nothing yet - the owed contract is five parts: (a) stamp every calibration with wall-clock time AND a boot-session id, warning loudly on reuse across a reboot or beyond an age threshold; (b) mark each component measured|preset individually and warn on any MIXED state, since partial calibration must be as visible as no calibration; (c) give the uncalibrated state the same prominence the [calibrated] tag gets; (d) re-measure by default in bench paths rather than on request; (e) diagnose the disk probe before any disk-tier number is quoted again.

contradictions.claim: THE 14-ROW LADDER MEDIAN HAS A RUN-TO-RUN NOISE FLOOR OF ROUGHLY +/-1 POINT, SO EVERY SUB-2-POINT 'IMPROVEMENT' THIS PROJECT HAS CLAIMED FROM IT IS UNSUPPORTED - INCLUDING TWO I MADE TODAY. Four ladders measured 2026-07-31 on the SAME idle machine with functionally equivalent calibrations returned medians of 7.2%, 7.9%, 8.8% and 9.0%. The final pair is the cleanest evidence: cal c24a253b (7.9%) and cal 2dc97d41 (9.0%) differ only in a disk figure that NONE of the 14 rows reads, yet the median moved 1.1 points and individual rows wandered 1-2 points in scattered directions (gemma4-12B measured 13.23 then 12.25 tok/s - a MEASUREMENT difference, not a prediction one). RETRACTED AT EQUAL PROMINENCE: I reported '7.2% beats the 8.8% baseline' and later '7.9%, beating the 8.8% baseline' as wins. Neither clears the noise floor. The ladder cannot resolve improvements below about 2 points, and any future claim from it must either exceed that or report repeated runs with a spread. This does NOT touch the large effects - RAM-only calibration at 12.5% and uncalibrated at 27.2% are far outside the floor and stand.

The +/-1 point figure is the observed spread across four passes, not a computed confidence interval - a proper estimate needs repeated passes under one fixed calibration, which has never been done.

Also argues for adding a DISK-TIER row to the ladder: all 14 current rows are VRAM or RAM-split, which is precisely how C-17's 6.8x-wrong disk probe survived undetected - a component no validation row reads can stay wrong indefinitely.

contradictions.claim: THE UPGRADE ADVISOR COULD ONLY EVER SUPPRESS GOOD UPGRADES, NEVER INVENT BAD ONES - a one-directional error, which is why it survived: every symptom looked like conservatism. upgrade_advisor() built its counterfactual by copying the baseline and overriding one resource key, but dropped n_layer and true_size_gb on the way in. evaluate() then re-derived both from presets, so the counterfactual was not the same model with more RAM - it was a DIFFERENT model. Two upgrades on unrelated resources could therefore land on the identical tok/s and both be reported, or a real gain could vanish into the re-derivation. Signature on the committed pre-fix artifact: llama-70b/colibri/ctx16384 printed '+16 GB RAM' and 'NVMe SSD' both at 0.5749513 tok/s. FIXED in 0782477 (identity carried at the function boundary). VERIFIED 2026-07-31 by a 340-cell re-sweep staked before it ran: 0 invented pairs against a live population of 24 cells where two different-resource upgrades both fire (so the check is not vacuous), 0 identity mismatches over 700 counterfactual evaluate() calls, 0 arithmetic mismatches over 131 fired upgrades. All 31 previously-affected cells named individually and clean. The auditor was falsified first: re-injecting the defect makes it exit 1 with 10 invented pairs, 700/700 identity mismatches and 51 arithmetic misses, and reproduces the 0.5749513 signature to six decimals.

contradictions.claim: THE DISK TIER IS PESSIMISTIC BY 30%: THE FIRST DISK-TIER MEASUREMENT THIS PROJECT HAS EVER TAKEN MISSED ITS OWN STAKED BAND, AND MISSED IT UPWARD. Predicted 0.331505 tok/s for Laguna-S-2.1-UD-Q2_K_XL (39.685 GB, 117.6B total / 8.14B active, -ngl 0) against a staked +/-25% band [0.265204, 0.442007]. Measured 0.476225 tok/s: err_pct -30.39%, OUTSIDE the band. KR1 FAIL, published at equal prominence and not renegotiated. THE MISS IS TRUSTWORTHY BECAUSE ALL THREE GUARD RULES PASSED FIRST - this is the difference between this run and the 2026-07-31 attempt, which produced a number 2.5% inside the band that had to be thrown away. KR3 (harness can vary): control 7B at -ngl 0 measured 7.570 tok/s against a 7.09 anchor and a >3.0 threshold, reps 7.5353/7.6048. KR4 (steady state): rep spread 1.172x (reps 0.5122/0.4369/0.4796) against a >2x kill rule - the contaminated run scored 2.09x here. KR2 (decode not load): tg32 0.449311 vs tg64 0.476225, 5.7% on one denominator and 6.0% on the other, so the ambiguity that could not be resolved on 2026-07-31 is moot at this margin. One cal_id (2dc97d41) at both ends, no C-14 warning, gates opened on the first attempt with CPU mean 0.2%/max 2.0% and 14.61 GB free. INVERTING THE TERM: the I/O component is 1.485x faster than modelled (predicted 2.66599 s of a 2.86572 s token; measured token 1.99486 s implies 1.79513 s of I/O). That resolves to exactly one of two things, and this measurement CANNOT distinguish them: either effective disk bandwidth under llama.cpp's sequential streaming is ~0.698 GB/s rather than the 0.47 GB/s the random-offset cold probe measures - i.e. the probe measures the wrong ACCESS PATTERN, a different error from the page-cache one C-17 fixed - or the page-cache miss fraction is ~0.429 rather than the modelled 0.637, which is what expert-usage skew would predict if hot experts stay resident and never pay disk. [RESOLVED HALFWAY by prereg #94, 2026-08-01: the access-pattern arm is REFUTED (see D-28) - scattered and contiguous reads measure 0.452 vs 0.459 GB/s, a 1.015x ratio, and both sit within 4 percent of the calibrated 0.47, which independently CONFIRMS the C-17 correction. The 30 percent miss therefore belongs to the miss fraction: modelled 0.637, implied ~0.429. Still an elimination, not a direct measurement of skew.]

Not covered: any disk-tier row at nonzero context depth (plan.py carries a KV-residency-deficit disclosure that stays untested here, KV ~12 MB at ctx 0); the printed WINNER row 'stream from disk (VRAM+RAM expert cache)' at 0.367424 tok/s, which needs a ktransformers/colibri-class runtime this box does not have and remains unmeasurable by nature rather than by scheduling. contradictions.claim: A LADDER MEDIAN CAN HOLD STILL WHILE EVERY SINGLE ROW UNDER IT MOVES. On 2026-08-01, on a box scrubbed idle (CPU mean 0.7%, max 2.0%, 14.11 GB free, gate open on the first attempt), ALL 14 ladder rows measured FASTER than the reference ladder taken under the same cal_id 2dc97d41 - not 13 of 14, all of them. Median +4.6%, range +1.4% to +27.5%. This is measured-vs-measured; prediction plays no part. Yet the median |err| moved only 9.0% -> 8.4%, because the errors are a MIX of signs and a uniform speed-up improves the rows we over-predict while worsening the rows we under-predict. The median was stable BY CANCELLATION, not because the machine was. CONSEQUENCE FOR C-18: the +/-1 point noise floor is real but it is the wrong instrument here - a median inside the floor is NOT evidence that the machine state is unchanged, and 'no regression' can be reported truthfully while the whole measurement basis has shifted underneath. The per-row measured-vs-measured diff is the sensitive detector; the median is not. RELEASE CONSEQUENCE, recorded so it cannot be quietly ignored: the 8.4% median PASSES its staked band [6.8, 10.8] and is being reported as UNCHANGED, not as an improvement, per C-18. SEPARATE OBSERVATION, AND THE FIRST VERSION OF IT WAS WRONG - RETRACTED HERE AT EQUAL PROMINENCE. I wrote: 'gemma4-12B has now returned 13.23, 12.25 and 15.62 tok/s across three runs - a 27% spread. That row is not measuring a stable quantity and its ladder entry should not be trusted.' I had picked THREE readings out of SEVEN. Pulling every archived ladder (2026-08-02) gives: 13.23 partial-disk cal, 12.66 idle pre-reboot, 12.17 post-reboot stale cal, 12.50 RAM-only cal, 12.19 uncalibrated, 12.25 locked baseline - six wildly different machine and calibration states spanning 12.17-13.23, a 1.087x spread. THAT IS A STABLE ROW, and one of the steadiest on the ladder. The seventh reading, 15.62 from the scrubbed-box unattended run, sits 1.18x above the cluster maximum. So the correct statement is not 'the row is unreliable' but 'ONE measurement is anomalous and unexplained' - a different claim with a different fix. Note what it is anomalous IN: that same run is the one where all 14 rows measured faster, and gemma was its LARGEST mover at +27.5%. A dense 12B split between VRAM and RAM has the most to gain from page-cache residency, which is exactly what U-37's residency-pressure hypothesis predicts - so this may be the same effect seen from a different angle rather than a defect at all.
contradictions.magnitude: 14/14 rows faster, median +4.6% (min +1.4%, max +27.5%), while median |err| moved 0.6 points
contradictions.evidence: weights/data/unattended_20260801_002809_ladder_result.json vs _ladder_baseline_backup.json (both cal 2dc97d41); gate readings in _RESULT.json; runner weights/unattended_serial.py
contradictions.scope: One machine, one pair of ladder passes. The DIRECTION is unambiguous (14/14 is not a coin flip) but the CAUSE is not established: the idle scrub, thermal state, page-cache warmth and Windows service state all changed together and were not varied independently. It is NOT established that the baseline was contaminated - only that the two passes are different machine states. Which one better represents a user's box is an open question with a practical answer: the scrubbed state is the ceiling, and a user with a browser open will not reach it.
contradictions.wired_into: reporting discipline, immediately: (a) every ladder comparison must print the per-row measured-vs-measured diff alongside the median, since the median can hide a uniform shift; (b) published headline speeds stay at the reproducible-by-others range, NOT the scrubbed-box ceiling - README's 20.4-22.2 for Qwen3-30B-A3B is retained even though this pass measured 22.94, because a user cannot reproduce a number that required stopping services to obtain.

contradictions.claim: THE DISK BANDWIDTH THE DRIVE DELIVERS AND THE DISK BANDWIDTH llama.cpp ACHIEVES ARE DIFFERENT NUMBERS, AND LAW 4 USES THE WRONG ONE. Raw reads on this drive measure 0.452-0.459 GB/s (D-28, sequential and scattered alike). llama.cpp streaming the same drive through mmap achieves an effective 0.2505 GB/s - a 1.82x gap. Measured by taking Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B Q3_K_M (13.7 GB, fits this 16 GiB box) from evicted to fully resident: cold 1.2997 tok/s with 0.16708 GB/token off disk, resident 9.09-10.00 tok/s with ZERO disk traffic. The whole difference in token time, 0.76939 s vs 0.1026 s, is attributable to 0.16708 GB of disk traffic, which prices that traffic at 0.2505 GB/s. THIS SUPPLIES THE MISSING COST C-21 AND #95 TRIANGULATED: #95 showed the law budgets ~2.7x too many bytes (R=0.366) while the row is only 1.485x fast, leaving ~0.789 s per token unexplained. A streaming rate 1.82x below the raw rate is the right size and sign to be it. WHAT I WITHDRAW: I staked this as a PER-FAULT LATENCY hypothesis and the scorer printed 'H4 SUPPORTED, lambda 16.35 us/fault, r2 1.000'. That verdict is NOT EARNED and I am retracting it rather than banking it. Fault counts were DERIVED as bytes/4096, never counted, so lambda*faults is identically bytes/(4096/lambda) - the per-fault model and a lower-effective-bandwidth model are the SAME equation in different units, and no experiment of this shape can separate them. 4096/16.35us is exactly the 0.2505 GB/s above. Two further weaknesses in my own design, recorded because the printed r2 hides them: the fit had only TWO DISTINCT x values (40791 and 0, three times), so it is a difference of means wearing a regression's clothes and r2=0.9999 is decorative - a line through two x values always fits; and KR-E, the out-of-sample check meant to falsify the LINE, held out a zero-fault run, so it only ever tested whether the resident time is stable run-to-run. The 6.7% it passed at is a real fact about run-to-run stability and no evidence at all for a fault model.
contradictions.magnitude: llama.cpp mmap streaming 0.2505 GB/s vs 0.452-0.459 GB/s raw on the same drive (1.82x)
contradictions.evidence: weights/exp96b_fault_latency.py + weights/data/exp96b_fault_latency.json (5 runs, evicted -> resident); weights/exp96_fault_latency.py + weights/data/exp96_fault_latency.json (the null that forced the redesign); raw-read baseline in weights/data/exp94_access_pattern.json
contradictions.scope: One drive, one model, one runtime, cold-vs-resident rather than a graded residency sweep. The MECHANISM is undetermined and this design cannot determine it: per-fault latency, mmap page-fault overhead, readahead defeat, and simply lower achieved throughput are all indistinguishable when fault count is derived from byte count. Separating them needs actual fault counts (ETW / hard-fault counters) or a runtime knob such as --no-mmap on a model small enough to load that way. CONTENTION: an agent was active, so 0.2505 GB/s is a LOWER bound on achieved streaming and the 1.82x gap is an UPPER bound. The clean-conditions disk row (0.476 tok/s) is consistent with it but was not measured with the disk counter running. NOT a coefficient: two independent routes now point near this number, but neither was measured clean, and C-02 is the standing warning against fitting a constant to convenient points.
contradictions.wired_into: nothing yet. The tempting move - reprice the disk tier at ~0.25 GB/s - would fix C-21's 30% miss in one line and is exactly the move this register exists to slow down: it would bake a contended measurement of one model on one drive into every disk-tier prediction. Owed first: (a) re-measure streaming efficiency under clean conditions with the disk counter live, (b) a second drive or model to show the 1.82x is not device-specific, (c) actual hard-fault counts to settle the mechanism. Until then plan.py keeps under-predicting the disk tier and the CHANGELOG says why.

contradictions.claim: A SINGLE-SAMPLE DISK PROBE SHIPS PAGE CACHE AS DISK BANDWIDTH, AND IT IS NOT AN EDGE CASE - IT IS 1-IN-8 EVEN ON A FILE YOU HAVE JUST DELIBERATELY EVICTED. The shipped measure_disk() took one timed read and its own docstring instructed the USER to 'treat a single number above ~1.5 GB/s as evidence of a warm cache rather than a fast disk'. Asking the caller to perform the check the code should do is not a guard, and hours after that sentence was written verify.py caught it live: reads of [0.413, 3.171, 0.415] GB/s on one file because an experiment had streamed 15 GB of it minutes earlier. MEASURED (prereg #97, 8 draws per arm on a 13.7 GB GGUF): with 73% of the file deliberately warmed, 6 of 8 single draws returned >1.5 GB/s, max 2.854 - RAM reported as disk, a 6.3x error. After evicting 16 GB of an UNRELATED file, 1 of 8 draws still came back at 2.092, a 4.7x error. The minimum over the draws was 0.4499 and 0.4537 in the two arms - both correct against D-28's independent raw-read baseline of 0.452-0.459, and 0.8% apart despite wildly different cache states. FIXED: measure_disk now returns the MINIMUM over N disjoint random regions, because nothing reads faster than the device except cache. THE SECOND HALF OF THE FINDING IS THE ONE THAT GENERALISES: a cold read cannot be GUARANTEED on this box at all, so single-sample probing is structurally unreliable rather than merely unlucky-after-a-download. P3 REFUTED, published rather than quietly dropped: I staked that a max/min > 2.0 spread test would flag warm files and stay silent on cold ones. It fired on BOTH arms - correctly, because neither arm was truly cold. The warm FRACTION does discriminate (1/8 evicted vs 7/8 warmed) but was chosen after seeing those numbers; it is reported to the user, labelled post-hoc, and never used to alter the estimate. ALSO PUBLISHED: run 1 of #97 scored P1 FAIL / P2 UNINFORMATIVE / P3 FAIL entirely because of three flaws in MY harness - P1 compared the min to the MEAN, which is inflated by the very outlier under study; and 3 GB warmed on a 37 GB file gives a random 512 MB draw an 8% hit rate, so the failing input was never constructed. The metric and the lever were fixed; every threshold (20%, 1.5, 1.0, 2.0x) stands exactly as staked.
contradictions.magnitude: 6/8 warm draws >1.5 GB/s (max 2.854, 6.3x error); 1/8 even after eviction (4.7x); min-of-N correct in both arms
contradictions.evidence: weights/exp97_warm_cache_guard.py + weights/data/exp97_warm_cache_guard.json; raw-read baseline weights/data/exp94_access_pattern.json; the live catch is in the 2026-08-01 verify.py failure recorded in the session commits
contradictions.scope: One drive, one box, two file sizes. The 1-in-8 residual-warm rate is specific to this machine's cache state and is NOT a general constant - what generalises is the direction (cache only ever inflates) and the estimator that follows from it. N=5 is a cost/confidence choice, not a measured optimum. The warm-fraction disclosure is post-hoc and unconfirmed on an independent run.
contradictions.wired_into: quantprobe/detect.py measure_disk (minimum of N, detail= returns the draws and warm count), quantprobe/calibrate.py and detect.run() now print the draws instead of asking the user to judge them. Guarded by tests/smoke.py t_p97_disk_probe_returns_the_cold_draw_not_the_warm_one, which is fixture-free and mutation-verified: it fails against the pre-#97 single-sample code by construction. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: nudging the probe toward the ~0.25 GB/s llama.cpp actually achieves (C-23). That gap is a runtime inefficiency and belongs in the law, not in a probe measuring the device; letting a mis-measured probe cancel an unmodelled cost is the mutually-consistent-presets trap C-17 exists to warn about.

contradictions.claim:
A BENCHMARK'S HEADLINE NUMBER CAN BE A PROPERTY OF ITS SCORER RATHER THAN OF ANY MODEL, AND THE TELL IS A UNIFORM EXACT ZERO ACROSS UNRELATED MODEL SIZES. Three independent instances inside one eval suite, each of which cost a spent row before it was noticed by hand: (1) hendrycks MATH-500 extracts the candidate answer as everything between the FIRST $ and the LAST $ of the response and never inspects \boxed{} - the 0.6B scored 0.00% while 89.4% of its answers carried a well-formed boxed value; (2) zero-shot AIME's prompt requests no answer format at all, so the 4B wrote a bare 'Answer: 49' in 30 of 30 items and scored 0 while the 0.6B happened to box out of habit; (3) lm-eval's gsm8k_cot_zeroshot strict-match filter requires the literal sentence 'The answer is N.', which that task's own doc_to_text ('Q: {question}
A: Let's think step by step.') never asks for - the pattern is inherited from the FEW-SHOT variant, where the exemplars demonstrated it, and stripping the exemplars removes the only thing that established the convention. MEASURED on case 3: 0 of 3,957 responses across three unrelated models (0.6B, 4B, 7B) match the strict pattern - not a low rate, exactly zero - while flexible-extract on the identical responses gives 36.8% / 81.7% / 79.9%. Inspected samples confirm the models answer correctly in prose ('Therefore, Janet makes $18 every day at the farmers' market.'). THE GENERALISATION IS THE VALUE: real capability differences do not line up on 0.0000 across a 0.6B and a 30B. A format mismatch produces exactly that, because the extractor never fires at all, and that sharpness is what makes the rule mechanical rather than a judgement call. NOT OUR BUG in case 3 - gsm8k-cot-zeroshot ships this way in lm-evaluation-harness 0.4.12 and anyone reporting its strict-match on a chat model is reporting a zero they did not earn. WHY THIS CLASS KEEPS HAPPENING, asked by Federico and worth recording as the mechanism rather than the symptom. FIRST: the output-format contract used to live in the FEW-SHOT EXEMPLARS. Every one of these scorers was built when benchmarks ran few-shot against base models, and the exemplars did double duty - teach the task AND demonstrate the answer format. Zero-shot chat evaluation deleted the exemplars and kept the scorer. GSM8K strict-match still demands 'The answer is N.' and nothing asks for it; hendrycks MATH-500 still slices $...$ and nothing asks for it. The contract was never written down anywhere, so removing it was invisible. SECOND, and this is the one that cost the most: THE ERROR ONLY EVER POINTS DOWN, AND LOW SCORES ARE PLAUSIBLE. A format mismatch cannot inflate a score, only destroy it, and 'small model bad at competition maths' is a believable story. The 0.6B's 0.00% on MATH-500 survived three protocol versions on exactly that plausibility. Had it scored 95% it would have been torn apart in ten minutes. WE AUDIT SURPRISING-GOOD FAR HARDER THAN SURPRISING-BAD, and this entire bug class only produces surprising-bad. THIRD: a format mismatch returns a NUMBER, not an error - no exception, no crash, nothing for a mechanical check to catch. QUANTIFIED across all 12 boxed rows: of the items not scored correct, 649 were graded-and-wrong and 172 were never gradeable at all (21%). So the models really are mostly wrong - but the unreadable share is wildly concentrated, and where it concentrates it dominates (4B on AIME: 43.3% unreadable against 6.7% graded-wrong). THE FOURTH MODEL CHANGED WHAT THIS FINDING IS. Qwen3-Coder-30B landed 2026-08-09 and scores 24.5% on GSM8K strict-match - not 0.0%. It writes the literal sentence 'The answer is N.' in 356 of 1,319 responses (27.0%); the 0.6B, 4B and 7B write it in exactly 0 of 3,957. So strict-match is not zero BY CONSTRUCTION, it is a PHRASING LOTTERY, and one model happens to hold a ticket. THE CONSEQUENCE IS WORSE THAN A DEPRESSED SCORE. On strict-match the 30B beats the 4B 24.5% to 0.0% - a 24.5-point rout. On flexible-extract, the SAME RESPONSES give 82.6% and 81.7%: a dead heat. One filter choice does not merely lower both numbers, IT INVERTS THE RANKING, and it does so with the confident appearance of a decisive result rather than the obvious wrongness of a zero. A reader shown the strict-match column would conclude the larger model is far better at grade-school maths. It is not; it is better at a sentence. AND THE NEAR-MISS IS THE LESSON: had the 30B row run FIRST, the uniform-zero detector this finding created would never have fired - the metric would not have been uniformly zero, only mostly - and the inverted ranking would have shipped. The detector catches the loud version of this failure. The quiet version, where one model's phrasing habit manufactures a 24-point lead, needs the extraction rate reported beside the accuracy, which is the only thing that makes 24.5-vs-82.6 legible as a gap between 'what we could read' and 'what was there'.
contradictions.magnitude: 0 of 3,957 responses match strict-match across 0.6B/4B/7B; the same responses score 36.8/81.7/79.9% under flexible-extract | 30B: strict-match 24.5% vs flexible-extract 82.6% on the same responses; writes the demanded sentence in 27.0% of them. Strict-match ranks 30B over 4B by 24.5 points where the honest gap is 0.9.
contradictions.evidence: weights/data/ev1/{0.6B,4B,7B}/gsm8k_cot_zeroshot/**/samples_*.jsonl and results_*.json; the strict pattern is filter_list[0] of lm_eval/tasks/gsm8k/gsm8k-cot-zeroshot.yaml (metadata version 3.0). Cases 1 and 2 are recorded in the EV-1 protocol v3 amendment and weights/lm_eval_tasks/math500_utils.py. FLEXIBLE-EXTRACT AUDITED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because C-26 showed our own scorer could be the defect and reporting a substitute metric without checking it would repeat the mistake one column over. flexible-extract takes the LAST number-like token anywhere in the response, which can fail both ways - a correct model that signs off after its answer, or a wrong one whose last token happens to be the gold value. An independent re-implementation over all 3,957 responses reproduces lm-eval's scores exactly (36.8 / 81.7 / 79.9) and agrees with the number on the FINAL LINE - where an answer normally lives - at 36.8 / 81.7 / 79.8%. Only 0.2-0.7% of responses disagree with the final line at all, and exactly one of those changes a verdict: doc 1170, whose final line is a bare LaTeX close-bracket with no number, so reaching back was correct. The substitute metric is sound on this corpus.
contradictions.scope: Three tasks in one suite on one harness version. The uniform-zero RULE is a heuristic with a stated false-negative: a scorer that is merely biased rather than totally broken produces low nonzero scores and slips through. It also cannot distinguish an artifact from a genuine capability wall - which is why the guard refuses and demands a human verdict rather than substituting a metric on its own. Two models are not enough to trigger it; coincidence is possible at n=2.
contradictions.wired_into: weights/ev1_report.py - check_publishable() raises SuspectMetric on any metric that is exactly 0.0 across >= 3 models unless the mechanism is recorded in ARTIFACTS, and REPORTED pins one publishable metric per task with the reason attached (GSM8K -> flexible-extract). Guarded by tests/smoke.py t_a_metric_that_is_zero_for_every_model_is_never_published, mutation-verified in three directions: neutering the guard, reverting GSM8K to strict-match, and an over-eager guard that fires on ragged real scores all turn the test red.

contradictions.claim: OUR OWN EXTRACTOR SCORED CORRECT ANSWERS AS ZERO, AND C-25'S DETECTOR COULD NOT SEE IT. math500_utils took the LAST \boxed in a response, inheriting lm-eval's last_boxed_only_string, which returns None when that box is unbalanced. Qwen3.5-4B reaches the correct answer on AIME and then enters a degenerate repetition loop - one response carries 683 occurrences of \boxed{116} - until generation is cut off at the token cap mid-token. The trailing fragment is unbalanced, the extractor returns None, and a response whose boxed value is EXACTLY the gold answer scores zero. Every missed case had the answer sitting in the box: gold 116/540/110/104/321 on AIME 2024 and 279/113/19/104 on AIME 2025, all graded wrong. FIXED: take the last WELL-FORMED box, scanning backwards. MEASURED over all 10 banked boxed rows (1,180 items): 9 answers rescued, 0 lost, and 8 of the 10 rows unchanged - the correction fires only where the defect occurs, which is the difference between a defect fix and a thumb on the scale. 4B AIME24 33.3% -> 50.0%, AIME25 36.7% -> 50.0%. THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST: C-25's rule - a metric that is EXACTLY 0.0 across three or more models - would never have caught this. The 4B's AIME rows were 33.3% and 36.7%, not zero; the loss was 5 items inside a plausible-looking score. A uniform zero is the loud version of this failure and we built a detector for the loud version only. The complementary check is per-item and cheap: a response containing a well-formed boxed value that the scorer reports as ungradeable is a scorer bug every time.
contradictions.magnitude: 9 of 1,180 items rescued, 0 lost, 8 of 10 rows unchanged; 4B AIME24 33.3 -> 50.0%, AIME25 36.7 -> 50.0%. One response held 683 repetitions of the same boxed answer.
contradictions.evidence: weights/data/ev1/4B/{aime24_boxed,aime25_boxed}/**/samples_*.jsonl - re-graded offline from the logged responses, no re-running. Fix and rationale in weights/lm_eval_tasks/math500_utils.py:last_well_formed_boxed; re-grading in weights/ev1_report.py:rescore_boxed. Original lm-eval verdicts are left untouched on disk so the delta stays auditable. CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER CLAIM IN THIS ENTRY'S OWN COMMIT: the samples are NOT committed. I wrote that the re-grade 'can be checked by anyone with the samples, which are committed' and then found, doing a pre-push audit, that weights/data/ev1 was ignored in its entirety - the .gitignore exceptions under weights/data match only files sitting directly in it, and these live four directories down. So KR-E1's 'result JSONs committed raw' was ALSO being violated silently, by a rule nobody had read against the stake. The 17 results_*.json are committed now (0.1 MB). The samples_*.jsonl are 42.8 MB - 15.6 MB for the boxed tasks this correction actually rests on, 19.9 MB of it GSM8K alone - and putting that in git history permanently is a repo decision for Federico, not one to make while tidying. Until it is made, the honest statement is: the re-grade is reproducible by anyone who RE-RUNS the suite, and directly checkable only by someone with local access to the samples.
contradictions.scope: One extractor, one model family, one failure shape (repetition into the token cap). The correction is only reachable because --log_samples kept every raw response; a suite run without it cannot be re-graded and its numbers are frozen at whatever the scorer of the day decided. NOT claimed: that 50.0% is the 4B's ceiling - a model that loops into the cap is still losing items to the loop itself, and a larger budget might score higher. The AIME rows also carry a budget disparity (7,168 tokens for 0.6B/4B/7B vs 8,192 for the 30B after a slot-plan change), which favours the 30B and is disclosed on the chart. KR-E1 BREACH, DECLARED RATHER THAN DEFENDED: prereg 2026-08-06 staked 'scorer is lm-eval as pinned - no post-hoc metric edits', and this correction is a post-hoc metric edit, made after seeing the numbers, that raised a headline. The rule exists because 'we fixed the scorer and the score went up' is exactly what a thumb on the scale sounds like from outside, and good faith is not visible from there. So both numbers ship: as-run 33.3% / 36.7%, re-graded 50.0% / 50.0%, on the chart and in a dated prereg amendment. contradictions.claim: FOUR 30B AIME ROWS DIED OF A PIPE-BUFFER DEADLOCK IN OUR OWN RUNNER, AND WE BLAMED THE SOFTWARE UNDER TEST TWICE BEFORE LOOKING AT OURSELVES. run_watched ran the child with stdout=PIPE and stderr=PIPE and then polled in a sleep loop, reading nothing until communicate() after exit. The OS pipe filled, lm-eval blocked in write(), stopped issuing HTTP requests, and the parent waited on a poll() that could never return. Captured live at 02:51 on 2026-08-09: port 8093 LISTENING with ZERO established connections, both python processes burning 0.00s of CPU over 15 seconds, llama-server idle at 607 MHz, and the server's last line a clean release of task 93152 after 24 of 30 items. PROVEN, not argued: the pre-fix pattern against a child writing 2 MB deadlocks (still running after 25s), the same loop writing to a FILE finishes in 0.5s with all 2,000,000 bytes captured. PROVENANCE: introduced in fad66d1, which replaced subprocess.run(capture_output=True) with a Popen poll loop in order to add the progress watchdog. subprocess.run was safe only because communicate() drains both streams on reader threads; hand-rolling the loop silently removed a guarantee nobody had written down. Both 30B MATH-500 rows that SUCCEEDED ran before fad66d1; every AIME attempt ran after it. THE TWO MISDIAGNOSES ARE THE FINDING. First it was called an lm-eval concurrency bug. Then a slot-plan problem, and an entire attempt was spent at ctx 16384 x 1 slot to prove it - which wedged at 24 of 30 with num_concurrent=1, where no race between generations is possible. That result refuted the theory outright and was read instead as a worse deadlock. The discriminator was in the first capture and was not used: A CLIENT THAT HOLDS NO SOCKET AND BURNS NO CPU IS NOT RACING, IT IS BLOCKED. Racing produces contention - connections, CPU, interleaved log lines. Blocking produces silence. Those are opposite signatures and we had the silent one on file three attempts before the cause was found.
contradictions.magnitude: 4 rows lost, ~9 hours of GPU time, 2 wrong diagnoses. Pre-fix: deadlock on a 2 MB child. Post-fix: 0.5s, 2,000,000 bytes captured.
contradictions.evidence: weights/data/ev1_deadlock_attempt4.txt (live capture: sockets, CPU, completion count, generation-length distribution). Introduced in fad66d1; fixed in weights/ev1_run.py run_watched. The successful 30B MATH-500 rows at 2026-08-07 23:04 and 2026-08-08 04:41 both predate fad66d1 (2026-08-08 05:18); every AIME attempt postdates it.
contradictions.scope: One runner, one OS. Windows pipe buffers are a few KB to 64 KB, so the threshold is platform-specific - but the defect is not: any poll loop over a PIPE that is not drained concurrently has this bug on every platform, and only the size of the child's output decides when it bites. NOT claimed: that the 30B AIME row will now complete. That is the next measurement, and it is running.
contradictions.wired_into: weights/ev1_run.py run_watched gives the child a FILE instead of a pipe - no buffer to fill, no reader thread to get wrong, and the harness output lands on disk for every row rather than only the ones that fail. AIME reverted to ctx 8192 x 2, the plan every banked row used, which also removes the 7168-vs-8192 budget disparity the wrong fix had introduced. Guarded by tests/smoke.py t_a_chatty_child_cannot_deadlock_the_watchdog: it runs a 2 MB child through the real run_watched with a 120s join timeout, because against the pre-fix code the failure is a HANG rather than an assertion - a test that hangs the suite teaches nobody anything. REPO-WIDE AUDIT, because one fixed call site is not a fixed class: t_no_runner_polls_a_pipe_it_never_drains walks every .py and flags any Popen(PIPE) with a .poll() between it and the drain. It found two more live sites - exp96_fault_latency.py and exp96b_fault_latency.py - both now writing to a temp file. Neither was infinite: watch()'s own 1800-2400s cap would have returned, which is arguably worse than a hang because the result is a measurement window silently containing a stalled child rather than an obvious failure. The check parses with ast rather than scanning text - a regex version reported the guard's own docstring as an offender, since prose describing the defect contains the same tokens as the defect.
contradictions.priority: high - it cost four rows and, worse, sent two investigations in the wrong direction

contradictions.claim: SIX DEFECTS IN ONE NIGHT, EVERY ONE FOUND BY CHECKING THE ARTIFACT RATHER THAN THE CODE - AND EVERY ONE INVISIBLE TO THE CODE-LEVEL CHECK THAT WAS ALREADY IN PLACE. The pattern is worth more than any of the individual bugs. In each case a guard existed and passed, because it tested INTENT; the defect lived in what the machine actually produced. (1) C-25, GSM8K: the task config looked right; reading 3,957 logged RESPONSES showed 0 matched the scorer's pattern. (2) C-26, our extractor: build_cmd was correct and the score was plausible at 33.3%; reading the responses showed the gold answer sitting in a box the scorer discarded. (3) C-27, the pipe deadlock: the runner's logic read fine; netstat and CPU time showed a client holding no socket and burning nothing, which is blocked, not racing. (4) Lock drift: a careful 2026-08-08 survey of 'the runners' passed; walking every .py found three more, including the RELEASE GATE at 3 of 5 and p0_lanes at 1 of 5. (5) KR-E1: .gitignore intent was 'keep the JSONs'; `git ls-files` returned zero, because the exceptions matched only files directly in weights/data. (6) The Phase B ledger: the field is called `reasons` and the media plan promised '4,551 exclusions by reason'; len(reasons) is 50, and the arithmetic not closing was the only tell. THE RULE: A CHECK THAT READS THE CODE TESTS WHAT YOU MEANT. ONLY A CHECK THAT READS THE ARTIFACT TESTS WHAT HAPPENED. Where an artifact exists - a logged response, a socket table, a git index, a length - read it. Where the two can diverge, they eventually will, and the code-level check will keep passing while they do.
contradictions.magnitude: 6 defects in one session; 4 had passing guards over them at the time. Cost before discovery: 4 GPU rows and ~9 hours (C-27), 9 mis-scored answers on a published headline (C-26), one chart nearly built on 1.1% of its data.
contradictions.evidence: C-25, C-26, C-27 registered separately with their own mechanisms and mutation-checked guards. Lock drift: tests/smoke.py t_every_runner_guards_against_every_other_lock, widened 2026-08-09 from a hand-listed set of runners to a walk of every .py, which found verify.py/gridbench.py/p0_lanes.py within seconds. KR-E1: 17 results_*.json now tracked. Ledger: weights/decon.py screen_batch, cap removed.
contradictions.scope: One project, one night, six instances - a pattern observed, not a law measured, and it is recorded as a working method rather than a finding about the world. The obvious counter-pressure is cost: artifact checks are slower to write and slower to run than reading a function, which is exactly why the code-level version gets written first and then trusted. NOT claimed: that code-level guards are worthless. Every one of them still holds the line it was written for; the point is that the line was drawn around intent.
contradictions.wired_into: The artifact-level checks added this session, each of which reads output rather than source: ev1_report.verify_prompts (what the models were SENT, from the logged prompts, and the capability chart refuses to render on a violation), ev1_report.rescore_boxed (re-grades from logged responses, provenance recorded), ev1_score.py (KR-E3 response health and P-E2, from the samples), tests/smoke.py t_no_shipped_chart_has_text_running_off_its_canvas and t_shipped_markdown_carries_no_invisible_control_characters (read the rendered SVG/MD, not the generator), t_no_runner_polls_a_pipe_it_never_drains and the widened lock guard (walk the repo, do not enumerate by hand), and t_findings_md_is_regenerable_and_matches_the_register (compare the generated file to what the generator produces now).
